elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause after § 9.3: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor" — covers both the Agreement and any Order Form.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor" — exactly 30 days, written, and no additional conditions or approvals attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall refund, on a pro-rata basis, all prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination" — express pro-rata basis and covers all prepaid Fees, curing the recurring-only limit in § 10.2.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term." No other retained provision (9.1 breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 Customer-only) grants Vendor a no-cause exit.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right runs on thirty days' notice, which is outside the 60–90 day fallback band (it is the stronger preferred position, not the fallback).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee, penalty or contingent payment is imposed on Customer's convenience termination anywhere in the redlined text, so the cap cannot be exceeded.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply in Customer's favour: Vendor is given no convenience right at all during a committed term, which is stricter than an end-of-term-only right; no retained clause reinstates one.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Vendor has no convenience termination right, so no notice period is required of it.

elements.element: Numbering of the inserted convenience clause
elements.evidence: The rationale and comment describe a new "§ 9.4", but the rendered paragraph appears unnumbered between 9.3 and 9.5; substantively operative either way, though the clause number should be applied on execution.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: all four preferred elements appear in operative language — a 30-day written-notice Customer convenience right over the Agreement or any Order Form, an express pro-rata refund of all prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term.
Fallback is incomplete only because the notice period is 30 days rather than 60–90 days; that is the stronger preferred position, so position-completeness is satisfied at the preferred level.

Minimality holds: the model language's surplus "in whole or in part" was correctly omitted, no survival tail, expense language, procedures or extra remedies were added, and the favourable existing § 9.5 (non-cascading termination, cumulative remedies) and § 10.2 refund floor were retained untouched.

The § 2.1 edit is necessary rather than cosmetic: the retained words "without reduction or termination rights" would directly contradict the new convenience right. The drafter deleted only the contradictory "or termination rights" and preserved the take-or-pay commitment and the no-reduction restriction, so the commercial minimum-spend mechanic survives.

Intent is preserved: no undefined term, dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence results. § 10.2's recurring-Fees refund remains as a floor for other termination routes and does not conflict with the broader convenience refund; § 8.2 non-renewal and § 27.3 force majeure exits are untouched.
Actionable cleanup (not a defect in substance): apply the clause number "9.4" to the inserted paragraph so the numbering sequence between 9.3 and 9.5 is intact in the executed document.
